- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +3–5% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +2–3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in catching the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving >2% from 30d mean, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases (last 7–10 days); add 0.3–0.8% buffer to end of forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underestimates; add 0.2–0.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
